source.body:
Managing your time with Kim Marshall and Jenn David-Lang https://gallery.mailchimp.com/3b9291b4f590f5a05b9e5cd8a/images/6968a1b6-b472-46c5-952e-0a0eb8d5657a.jpg https://gallery.mailchimp.com/3b9291b4f590f5a05b9e5cd8a/images/808f33b7-f49a-47ef-8f16-82d45e9a2007.jpg

PMP168: Managing Your Day with Kim Marshall and Jenn David-Lang

Podcast: Play in new window | Download
Subscribe: Apple Podcasts | Android

If you are like most school leaders, time management can be one of the most difficult parts of your work.

Most new school leaders I meet explain how overwhelming the list of to-do’s can be. What are the solutions? Well, Kim Marshall and Jenn David-Lang provide a wealth of information on resources and practices that work in managing your time.

Kim Marshall and Jenn David-Lang are the authors of the new book: The Best of the Marshall Memo, Book One: Ideas and Action Steps to Energize Leadership, Teaching, and Learning. In this week’s podcast episode, we discuss their chapter on Time Management with valuable takeaways, tips, and strategies.

Kim & Jenn Bios: https://williamdparker.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Kim_presenting_500.png

Kim Marshall

Kim was a teacher, central-office administrator, and principal in the Boston Public Schools for more than 30 years. He now leads workshops and courses, coaches school leaders, consults with schools and districts, and produces the weekly Marshall Memo, summarizing ideas and research from over 60 publications. He is the author of numerous articles and books, including Rethinking Teacher Supervision and Evaluation.

https://williamdparker.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Jenn-cropped-2-1200x675.png

Jenn David-Lang

Jenn has worked in education for more than 25 years as a teacher, administrator, and consultant. She now designs and provides workshops for principals and teachers, coaches leaders, and conducts school evaluations. Since 2007, Jenn has published The Main Idea, a service for busy school leaders that provides summaries of compelling education books, accompanied by suggestions for professional learning. She currently lives in Brooklyn, New York.

Kim Marshall and Jenn David-Lang are best know as “designated readers” for busy front-line educators, curating the best ideas and research from scores of magazines and books. In their new book, they identify the most thought-provoking and helpful article summaries from the Marshall Memo archive and add professional learning suggestions. The book aims to help principals, teachers, superintendents, consultants, and researchers address the most pressing issues they face every day.

https://williamdparker.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/marshallmemobook-1200x675.jpg

Check out the new book here!

Time Management Takeaways

In this episode, we explore one area of their research and practice: How Leaders Can Grow in Time Management.

Principals and school leaders share a common frustration with time management. How can you accomplish so many responsibilities and tasks? Kim and Jenn share lessons they’ve learned from your research and practice, including:

  • Understanding your time while knowing you’ll never check off all the blanks
  • Studying the “rock analogy“: Big rocks first, then gravel, then sand, then water… (When you prioritize important tasks first, you can add much more that matters to your day.)
  • Examining Stephen Covey’s 4 Quadrants:
  1. Important/Urgent
  2. Important/Not Urgent
  3. Not Important/Urgent
  4. Not Important/Not Urgent
  • Avoiding the useless: useless feedback, useless meetings, useless evaluation processes, and time-consuming emails
  • Utilizing Justin Baeder’s fire analogy: Fire fighters who work on prevention fight fewer fires so delegate, create committees, and train others to do tasks
  • Using whatever tool works for you to document and keep various ideas and requests in one place
  • Making a rainy-day list of ideas that don’t need to be worked on immediately
  • Reviewing your list at a scheduled time each week
  • Setting goals for each day, week, month and year

Staying Connected & Free Resources

Listen-in the full podcast of this conversation (or watch the video version) for in-depth feedback!

Also, Kim can be found at the MarshallMemo.com or at Kim.Marshall48@gmail.com. If you email him there, he will send you a free chapter on time management from the new book!

You can reach Jenn at TheMainIdea.Net for a free resource of David Allen’s tips for time management!

Mastermind Update

If you want to be a part of an exclusive community of other school leaders who meet on a weekly basis for leadership discussions, book studies, and hot-seat opportunities, you can learn more by visiting williamdparker.com/mastermind or email me at will@williamdparker.com.

The transformation of New Orleans to a system of charter schools has been a city- and community-supported effort designed around three principles: educator run schools, parent choice and public oversight. https://gallery.mailchimp.com/15e55bce3ca48391b8e2995d4/images/def22bf5-2b21-4beb-9d9b-a9269d8abf28.png 10 Turning Points: Why It’s Time to Lean Into The Opportunity of the Innovation Age

We’re in a new age—a new economy and a new ecology. How might we adjust our ways of thinking and the ways we share our planet to better lean into future opportunities? https://gallery.mailchimp.com/15e55bce3ca48391b8e2995d4/images/effffe5e-99fd-46ac-b6d3-31ad4f688141.jpeg Solving Interesting Problems With an Entrepreneurial Mindset

As the workplace continues to shift, leadership and agility are becoming necessary for all members of a team. An entrepreneurial mindset consists of many of the most useful skills for the future. And no, it doesn’t mean starting your own company. https://gallery.mailchimp.com/15e55bce3ca48391b8e2995d4/images/703c6a49-94da-4343-9e1b-fd37ffed23b8.jpg 11 Alternative Schools that are Real Alternatives

Trying to push all kids through a content-centric, compliance-oriented model just won’t work. A variety of alternative approaches have been attempted; here are a few approaches educators have to develop for youth that haven’t been successful in traditional schools.

LISTEN

https://gallery.mailchimp.com/15e55bce3ca48391b8e2995d4/images/be4df486-2462-4984-968b-7f7d7b7893d5.png

In this episode of the Getting Smart Podcast, Tom Vander Ark speaks with Dan Condon, the Associate Director of Professional at Eagle Rock School about community-connected project-based learning.

FINDINGS

A New Perspective on Student Success | A recent study by New Schools Venture Fund seeks to identify an expanded definition of student success (EDSS). Through surveying numerous schools and consulting additional resources, they have honed a list of skills and habits that further expand upon what constitutes student success. Email Reigns Supreme | A recent report by Project Tomorrow has identified that despite a push to use text and mobile apps for communication, 83% of parents prefer communicating with teachers via personal email. This indicates a continued emphasis on personal communication, rather than accessing data and information through a student portal. The Power of Empathy | Intentionally strengthening and building empathy is proving to be more essential than ever before. source.subject: Wednesday Innovation, presented by Sahn Ward Coschignano: In which octogenarians race, future doctors suit up and the Mouse House roars
source.body:
http://files.constantcontact.com/7c06501c401/f792d348-4578-43a5-9838-9573c08d6d6d.png

News, loose thoughts and opinion

from inside the new economy

Middle of the road: Welcome to Wednesday, dear readers, as we reach the midpoint of another busy week of socioeconomic innovation.


It’s Oct. 16 out there – Boss’s Day in the United States and Canada, when we salute the fair and loveable leaders who sign our checks and keep the ship on course.


Alternates: Those less eager to celebrate their supervisory situation might consider World Food Day, or perhaps World Anesthesia Day would help.


Gas man: Of course,World Anesthesia Day – a.k.a. Ether Day – marks the date in 1846 when Boston dentist William Morton first publicly demonstrated ether’s incapacitating capacities at Massachusetts General Hospital.


Well read: This is also a great date for classic English literature – both Charlotte Brontë’s “Jane Eyre” (1847) and C.S. Lewis’ “The Lion, The Witch and the Wardrobe” (1950) were published on Oct. 16, both in London.


“Jeopardy” champ Ken Jennings went there: Happy anniversary, Brigham Young University – the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints’ private research university was founded in Provo, Utah, as Brigham Young Academy on this date in 1875.


In control: Famed nurse Margaret Sanger, driving force behind the Planned Parenthood Federation of America, opened the first U.S. birth-control clinic in Brooklyn on Oct. 16, 1916.


It’s a small world after all: Now the happy public façade of a sinister technocratic regime controlling entertainment, news and critical commodities around the globe, Disney was founded on Oct. 16, 1925.


Long distance: And it was this date in 2016 when Ed Whitlock, aged 85, completed the Toronto Marathon in 3:56:36, setting the octogenarian world marathon record.


The late, great Canadian – who was finally stopped by prostate cancer in 2017, one week after his 86th birthday – was also the first person over 70 to finish a marathon in less than three hours (he did it three times), the world-record holder for over-70 marathoners (2:54:48, at age 73) and the oldest person, period, to run a marathon in less than three hours (2:58:40, at age 74).


Wilde child: Oscar Fingal O'Flahertie Wills Wilde (1854-1900) – Irish playwright, poet, novelist, essayist and convicted criminal (for “gross indecency with men”) – would be 165 years old today.


Also born on Oct. 16 were “father of Italian geology” Giovanni Arduino (1714-1795); lexicographer and dictionary namesake Noah Webster (1758-1843); American biochemist Henry Sherman (1875-1955), who established average human requirements for many vitamins and minerals; Bjorn Helland-Hansen (1877-1957), the Norwegian pioneer of modern oceanography; and groundbreaking American novelist Kathleen Winsor (1919-2003), whose “Forever Amber” was pretty racy for 1944.


Murder, she survived: And take a well-earned bow, Angela Lansbury – the iconic Irish-American thespian with an eight-decade career spanning theatre, film and, of course, insanely popular television turns 94 today.


Give your best to the TV sleuth, the vicar of vitamins and all the other Oct. 16 innovators at editor@innovateli.com – give us your story tips and calendar suggestions, please and thank you.



From our sponsor:Sahn Ward Coschignano is one of the region’s most highly regarded and recognized law firms. Our attorneys are thought leaders, dedicated to achieving success through excellence. With our broad experience in land use, development, litigation, real estate, corporate and environmental law, we have the vision and knowledge to serve our clients and our communities. Please visit www.swc-law.com.



BUT FIRST, THIS


Earnings potential: The State University of New York has introduced a new online tool offering a real-time rundown of SUNY graduate earnings.


The SUNY Gradwages interactive dashboard includes programmable parameters and a host of valuable data on what graduates from all 64 state university campuses earn, and in what fields, extending as far as 10 years after they leave the SUNY system. Combining academic information with wage statistics from the New York State Department of Labor, the dashboard lets users search by area of study, business sector or campus, and to filter their searches by degree types and other factors.


The idea was to create an “easy-to-use tool that will help both prospective and current students make informed choices about their majors and career path,” according to SUNY Chancellor Kristina Johnson. “SUNY Gradwages gives students and their parents an expectation of what they can earn years after college.”


Gold standard: Adelphi University will show its true colors as part of National Chemistry Week.

Created by Russian chemist Dimitri Mendeleev in 1869, the periodic table of elements turns 150 this year. To mark the anniversary, the New York section of the American Chemical Society has scheduled a National Chemistry Week celebration (Oct. 20-26), and as part of that celebration, more than 50 organizations from around the region are creating their own unique “element” for a giant, three-dimensional periodic table slated to be unveiled Friday at the New York Hall of Science in Queens.


Among the sections being donated is the periodic symbol for gold (Au), created by members of the Adelphi University community. Gold, of course, is Adelphi’s primary school color, making this “a great expression of their love for Adelphi … and a wonderful example of the collaboration between arts and sciences,” according to Adelphi associate chemistry professor Justyna Widera-Kalinowska, 2019 chairwoman of the NY-ACS.



TOP OF THE SITE


Critical connection: Ambitious We Connect the Dots hopes a new alliance with a Marcum marketing team will help proliferate its proven STEM-education model.


Coat drive: Diversity reigns as freshly minted Long Island medical students don their white coats and kick off their med-school journeys.


Stuck in Park: A new corporate identity couldn’t help Melville’s former Park Electrochemical Corp. gain altitude in its latest quarterly report.



VOICES


Bean counter: Pod people beware! Snooty Starbucks-ers stay away! Food and beverage baron Ambrose Clancy knows what makes a good cup of joe – and where to get it on Long Island. His latest Voices column here.



STUFF WE’RE READING


Imagination prioritization: According toForbes, business revolutions always come from new ideas.


Cultural phenomenon: Inc. travels deep inside Amazon, where a creative culture offers a blueprint for all disruptive companies.


Blame game: Yes, according to Entrepreneur, your company is discouraging innovation – and yes, it’s your fault.



RECENT FUNDINGS


+ RapidSOS, a New York City-based emergency technology company, closed a $55 million funding round led by Energy Impact Partners.


+ Satelles Inc., a Virginia-based provider of satellite-based time and location services, raised $26 million in Series C funding led by C5 Capital, with participation from Iridium Communications and existing investors.


+ Razberi Technologies, a Texas-based provider of secure video surveillance and IoT solutions, raised $5.8 million in funding led by LiveOak Venture Partners, Chartline Capital Partners and other investors, including the family offices of industry leaders Ken Boyda and Jiri Modry.


+ Swift Health Systems, a California-based maker of invisible orthodontic braces, raised $45 million in series C funding co-led by Vivo Capital, Novo Holdings and venBio Partners.


+ Mebias Discovery, a Pennsylvania-based drug-discovery biotech targeting G-protein-coupled receptors, closed a $3.5 million funding round led by Viva Biotech Ltd. and Sprout BioVentures.


+ Parsley Health, an NYC-based personalized holistic-health services startup, raised $26 million in Series B funding led by White Star Capital, with participation from FirstMark Capital, Amplo, Alpha Edison Partners, Arkitekt Ventures and Galaxy Digital.



BELOW THE FOLD


Lights: How to keep those screens from ruining your eyes (and your sleep).


Cameras: Apple and Google snark over computational photography.


Action: How bikers, hikers, skiers and climbers spread handcrafted beer across the land.


And … cut! That’s a print! Special thanks to the real stars – the amazing organizations that support Innovate LI, including Sahn Ward Coschignano, where the cutting-edge Environment, Energy and Resources practice group is ready for a close-up.

source.subject: Innovate 453: Nearpod expands to higher ed; The Internet of Things in schools
source.body:
Edtech insights for decision makers

https://go.edsurge.com/rs/590-LFO-179/images/newsletter_EdSurge_Logo_Green.png

No. 453 | October 16, 2019

View in Browser

Subscribe to this Newsletter »

https://go.edsurge.com/rs/590-LFO-179/images/newsletter_InnovateIcon.png

Innovate

Edtech insights for decision makers

This issue is sponsored by

https://go.edsurge.com/rs/590-LFO-179/images/boston%20college.png


As the old saying goes, reading is fundamental. As a text (if not exactly print) publication, we couldn’t agree more. But what does reading well look like? That’s the question explored by a new EdSurge guide of the same name. During the past few weeks, we’ve teased stories about silent reading, the impacts of smartphone culture and building up reader motivation. Now you can check out the full guide—with more stories to come. We promise it’s a good read.

EDPUNK UNDERGROUND

WHEN IoT MEETS I.T.: Sandra Paul doesn’t typically don a safety helmet and work boots for her job as a district director of information technology. But thanks to the “internet of things,” or IoT, she’s overseeing the installation of internet-connected boilers, lighting systems and more. It’s providing districts like hers with tangible benefits—but creating more work for IT in the process.

NEAR, FAR, WHEREVER YOU ARE: Nearpod boasts a far reach in the K-12 education market. But the provider of interactive lessons and assessment tools is now setting its sights higher—literally—by offering a bundle of services that college departments may already purchase separately. Will anybody bite?

CULTURE SHOCK: When new staff arrived to Langley Elementary in 2016, the school's suspension rate was at 66 percent and physical altercations were not uncommon. Three years and a top-to-bottom transformation later, the school is unrecognizable. EdSurge reporter Emily Tate recently visited the Washington, D.C. school to understand how a social-emotional learning-based approach changed school culture for the better.

Sponsored by Hāpara
DISORGANIZATION OR DIGITAL DISCONNECT?: “If schools want to empower 21st-century learners, the platforms they select must diminish the confusion and frustration that is happening with today’s students,” argues Hāpara's Lindsay Dixon Garcia. She offers tips for developing a digital classroom “that is every bit as organized as we expect the students themselves to be."

WEGROW NO MORE: The division of WeWork that operated a private elementary school will close its doors next year. “As part of the company’s efforts to focus on its core business, WeWork has informed the families of WeGrow students that we will not operate WeGrow after this school year,” a spokesperson told EdSurge. The move comes as WeWork looks to slash assets and staff after withdrawing its IPO plans.

CODING BOOTCAMP MEETS LIBERAL ARTS? Leaders at Davidson College noticed that some graduates felt the need to attend a high-cost coding bootcamp as a bridge to a tech job after earning their bachelor’s degrees. So the college decided to build its own intensive program in San Francisco inspired by bootcamps, but informed by the liberal arts.

Sponsored by Vivi
ARE YOUR CLASSROOM TOOLS A WISE INVESTMENT? “Talk with the trainers, the tech people and try the technology," advises Mark Rugg, who implemented Vivi’s classroom engagement solution after an earlier tech roll out failed his Utah district. The screen mirroring tool’s appeal to teachers was a “no brainer,” but he made sure it was also cost effective and a smart investment. Rugg shares his tips for district leaders as they consider technology purchases.

KA’CHING!

STELL-AR: The origins of Palo Alto-based Stellic can be traced to the work that cofounder Sabih Bin Wasi put into planning which college courses to take and when during his own academic career. Now, investors have taken note of his process, investing a $3.1 million seed round to help the startup make course scheduling easier for students all over.

The following is a message from our sponsor

https://go.edsurge.com/rs/590-LFO-179/images/BC%20Lynch%20Logo.png

Boston College Lynch School of Education and Human Development

The experientialMaster’s in Learning Engineering program prepares students to design engaging learning experiences and incorporate cutting-edge technologies through design studios, internships, and mentoring.

Scholarships for this one year full time program are still available. Join our webinar on Why we need Learning Engineers on November 13th. Register here.


Follow your EdSurge writers @tonywan, @jryoung, @stephenoonoo, @ByEmilyTate, @WadeMillward and @becky_koenig for the latest news and scoops as they hit the wire. And, of course, @EdSurge!

ON THE PODCAST

GOLDEN AGE OF TEACHING? Researchers are making new discoveries these days about how people learn, and some of those findings are making their way onto campuses in the form of new teaching practices. That has Duke University’s Matthew Rascoff excited about making wide-scale improvements in how colleges teach. Hear his thoughts on where he sees campus innovation going on this week’s podcast.

3R’S: RESEARCH, REPORTS & RESULTS

WORKING ENVIRONMENT: An edtech product that “works” in a study may not work in your school. That’s because existing research often pays scant attention to all the different variables that make each classroom environment unique, such as teacher buy-in, planning time and culture. But a new research competition from the U.S. Department of Education could change all that.

KEEP IN TOUCH: Reports of email’s death may be greatly exaggerated. That’s according to a newly released Project Tomorrow survey that found many parents still prefer it as a communication tool. But preferences vary based on age—with millennials favoring text messages. (Baby boomers? Not so much.) Check out what schools and companies can learn from the results.

HAPPY TEACHER PROJECT: Early childhood educators face many challenges, especially low compensation and poor benefits. However, Kyong-Ah Kwon, an associate professor at the University of Oklahoma, is focused on oft-neglected ingredients of a high-quality early childhood workforce: happiness and health. She’s leading an interdisciplinary group of experts to investigate the psychological, professional and physical aspects of teachers’ well-being.

Sponsored by D2L
TECH SUPPORT: “Technology can be a busy teacher’s trusted teaching assistant and an administrative best friend,” writes D2L’s Ellyn Winters-Robinson, but it “needs to be tightly woven into the learning pedagogy, guided by best practices for use.” Read her advice for effectively implementing technology to engage learners, simplify work flows and help teachers reclaim lost time.

EDSURGE UPDATES

BUZZ BUILDER If educators don’t understand the need for your product, they won’t try it. Get them talking about the issues your product solves and make thought leaders out of your executives at the same time—with an EdSurge webinar. Next month: History’s Not Static: Building a Social Studies Curriculum That Adapts and Endures, sponsored by Newsela.

MORE WHEELIN’ & DEALIN’

Riverside Insights, an Itasca, Ill.-based provider of assessment services to students and employees, has bought Educational Software for Guiding Instruction, an Elkhart, Ind.-based provider of a platform for teacher-led early childhood assessments.

Blue Canoe, a Bellevue, Wash.-based provider of an app for employees to learn English, has raised $2.5 million in equity financing from 20 investors, according to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filings.

Who knew that spell-check could be worth such a big check? Grammarly, the San Francisco-based provider of a digital writing assistant that provides feedback on spelling and grammar, has raised $90 million in its second fundraise, which was led by General Catalyst and IVP.

Element451, a Raleigh, N.C.-based company with a platform for college admission leads, has raised a $1 million seed round from startup accelerator and early-stage venture firm Cofounders Capital.

Sponsored by Reading Plus
AN EXPERT SHARES HIS SECRETS: The road to lifelong learning starts with proficient reading. But students’ reading motivation is often "shockingly low," says researcher John Guthrie, who spent 45 years studying student motivation and engagement. He shares his insights into the right—and wrong—ways to nurture a desire to read, including intrinsic motivation, text choice and real-life connections.

MOVERS & SHAKERS

Seth D. Harris, a former acting secretary of labor under the Obama administration, has joined education consultancy Whiteboard Advisors.

Tasha Kitty is now vice president of people at Panorama Education. She has served in similar roles for CyberArk, Horizons for Homeless Children and Digitas.

Want to share your new role? Or know of someone who’s ascended into the corner office? Let us know here!

ALSO ON OUR RADAR

A black hole took Fortnite offline Tuesday. The event presaged a major update. (New York Times)

New Jersey considers adding climate change to every subject area—but is there enough existing curriculum? (Chalkbeat)

Could Iowa become the next edtech hub? A new state report explores the outside possibility. (Cedar Rapids Gazette)

And of course, since your clips feed directly into your Airtable bases, it’s easy to filter and sort them later or look at them using different views.

Learn more


The web clipper block also has a special feature that allows you to share the clip recipes you create! We’ve even made a special section of the community forum dedicated to swapping clip recipes. Head on over there, share your best creation, and enter to win our latest contest: whoever cooks up the best clip action recipe will receive a pair of Airtable-branded Airpods!

Formatting fanatics, take note(s)! Our latest beta will allow you to:

  • Format your paragraphs with headers
  • Organize your ideas using bullet points, numbered lists, or checkboxes
  • And more!

source.subject: Simon Sinek on Leadership
source.body:
The world-renowned author of “Start with Why” has devoted his life to understanding, promoting and encouraging leadership. In this week’s episode... https://gallery.mailchimp.com/c0ee5092b4b144b9784fc8001/images/6e1bf315-0c5f-4550-a1f7-57222aacefaf.jpg

Dear David,

https://gallery.mailchimp.com/c0ee5092b4b144b9784fc8001/images/560b3639-1a08-48a0-b433-96865d1aa35b.jpg

“Be the leader you wish you had.”


In one sentence, Simon Sinek explains his life’s work so far. The world-renowned author of “Start with Why” has devoted his life to understanding, promoting and encouraging leadership. Now he has taken his considerable intellect and applied it to the problems plaguing businesses and employees.

His new book, “The Infinite Game”, describes the mindset necessary to build a truly great business.

“They don’t understand the game they’re in. Business is an infinite game. And when they play with a finite mindset lots of people suffer, including the companies they themselves are trying to build!”

https://gallery.mailchimp.com/c0ee5092b4b144b9784fc8001/images/64b49fd1-3e71-4d5e-b15f-db22c4951ad6.jpg

On this week’s episode of Impact Theory, Simon Sinek defines what an infinite game is. Then he explains that most businesses have gotten so far off course because they play the finite game of trying to meet quarterly earnings deadlines, instead of playing the infinite game of advancing a just cause that their employees can believe in.

Along the way, he goes deep on the subject of leadership. This is a fantastic episode to watch if you:

  • Know that something is terribly wrong in the company you work for, but you can’t quite identify what it is.
  • Want to become a leader but haven’t had role models or don’t know how.
  • Want to build the courage to thrive in a world that increasingly doesn’t know how to show people what real leadership is.


Click here to watch this week’s episode of Impact Theory with Simon Sinek, and start building an infinite mindset for a future that will require you to play “The Infinite Game.”

-The Impact Theory Team

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (PS/IS 155 PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (PS/IS 155 PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

Subject: FKL SonarCloud

Dear Mike and Tim,

I just listened to a voicemail from Tim stating that there is an issue with a payment. Please understand that in my role as an Assistant Principal for the Franklin K. Lane Campus, I do not have access to a budget, purchase orders, etc. The five Principals on the campus are cc’d.

The first mention of any billing situation to come to my attention was sent by Mike on 9/23/19:

Jim,

Let me also copy the account manager for FKL on this one.

We'll have to figure out the billing situation. Last time we did we tried to send an invoice after the fact and this probably wasn't the best way to do things. Can you send me which schools will be affected by the re-zoning so I can discuss with them the costs and get approvals before we proceed?

I just want to make sure we do it properly this year!

I responded within 10 minutes providing the information requested of me. On 9/25/19, I received this from Mike:

Hello all,

Sorry for the late response. I dropped the ball on this.

For us to come out to reprogram the PA system, it would be $300 per the requesting school affected. The cost isn't really based on the number of rooms affected, but the standard cost for the trip and reprogramming.

If this is agreeable, let us know, we can schedule to come out and do the reprogramming and send the proper invoices.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

So, to date, we are in process to discuss the receipt of a bill (or bills) for this $300 (x2 schools?) and the creation of a purchase order by the schools for the requested updates; this is on our agenda for discussion tomorrow morning and we should have an e-mail response by tomorrow afternoon.

As for any work done previously, I will state that the work Tim did at FKL was necessary to make the SonarCloud system work as described when purchased by the schools (e.g.: each individual school will have the ability to announce via SonarCloud to their respective “zoned” classrooms). I have no knowledge of any bills received by the schools here that are past-due, or how SonarCloud internal operations function in this regard – if SonarCloud has to pay a third-party vendor (or whatever the situation may be) to make their product function as described when it sold, then so be it.

I am happy to help in any way that I can, but I need to know that there is an issue first – had I been informed earlier, an e-mail similar to this one would have went out earlier. This email also serves to ensure that we are all on the same page, as the voicemail received suggests that we are not.

In any case, I look forward to working with both of you in the future.

Thanks,

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (PS 101 PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (PS 101 PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (Concord HS PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (Concord HS PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (PS 207X PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!
Hello Guys!

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

TRANSCRIPT INFORMATION

2019 Graduates: Your transcripts will be sent to your colleges on or before June 30.

Other transcript requests between June 12 and July 11: Please contact Mrs. Lopez, the Registrar, at dlopez1@sandi.net<mailto:dlopez1@sandi.net>.

Transcript requests AFTER July 11: Contact Student Records at studentrecords@sandi.net<mailto:studentrecords@sandi.net>.

La Jolla High School Registration Dates and Times 2019-2020

Please read the following information regarding the registration process. Your cooperation will help ensure a smooth process and minimize any delays as you move from station to station. Registration is ONLY for students currently enrolled at La Jolla High for the coming 2019-2020 school year. Students entering from 8th grade at Muirlands Middle School last year are enrolled. If you have recently moved into the area, please contact the school by phone beginning August 15 for enrollment requirements and appointments.

ALL ENROLLED STUDENTS MUST PARTICIPATE.
Registration must be completed by the student – parents may not substitute.
One student may not register for another student.

10th - 12th graders: On the assigned registration day, students should arrive at the following staggered times based on the first letter of their LAST NAME:

12th graders on August 19th
11th graders on August 20th
10th graders on August 21

A – C 8:00 am
D – H 8:30 am
I – M 9:00 am
N – R 9:30 am
S – Z 10:00 am

9th graders ONLY: All 9th graders participate in a special combined registration/orientation on August 22nd from 8 am-12:30 pm. During that time they will go through the registration process with the assistance of Link Crew (upperclassmen ambassadors).

PLEASE NOTE: Returning students should have turned in all registration documents at the end of last school year.
Students will not be able to complete this process if required forms are missing or incomplete.

Purchases can be made via our online store https://webstores.activenetwork.com/school-software/la_jolla_high_school/

You will find specific information regarding Athletics at www.LJVikings.com<http://www.ljvikings.com/>

Students who arrive BEFORE their designated time frame will be instructed to RETURN to campus at their assigned time. The registration process will take approximately two hours for 10th -12th graders. There will be plenty of volunteers to help each student through the process. Students not present for their assigned day will need to complete registration on one of the later registration dates. NO students will be permitted to gather on campus prior to 7:00 am….this will be strictly enforced.

Library Fines, Late Fines, Lost/Damage Charges, Late Book Return, and Missing/Lost Books can all be paid before registration day. The library will be open for book returns or debt payments from Monday, August 19th through Thursday, August 22nd, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. Please bring the notice you received in the mail, and remember to keep your receipt when paid.

For Lock & Locker Assignments: 10th, 11th, and 12th grade students can request locker assignments and a lock at the beginning of the school year. More information to come

9th Graders only: Locker Assignments will be given at Registration

Summer FAQ’s

Thanks so much for being part of the La Jolla High School community. We are privileged to work with your students and look forward to another wonderful school year. As we get ready for a new school year, we know families have many questions. We have developed this FAQ document to help address a variety of questions you may have. Please do not hesitate to contact our office staff if you still have any further questions. Again, our goal is to provide the highest level of educational experiences for your students. We know that our strong family-school-community partnership will continue to help our students be well prepared and extremely successful in whatever post K-12 opportunities await them.
Answers to the most often asked questions of new parents:
Please remember that most questions can be answered by looking at the school’s website, the PTSA website, the Foundation of LJHS website, and by reading the eNews. Also remember that there is a PTSA FB page and a LJHS College Info FB page.

FAQ SHEET – ARTICULATION - FEBRUARY – 2019
1. My student is not in Integrated Math I at Muirlands, can he take a placement test to enter into Integrated Math 2 as a freshman?
2. To progress to a higher level of math, a student must take the course over the summer. See Summer School slides in Articulation Powerpoint<https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.sandiegounified.org/schools/la-jolla/course-planningschedule-changes&sa=D&ust=1562009432469000>.
3. My student wants to take Integrated Math I or Integrated Math 2 this summer so he can skip a year ahead for 9th grade? Can they? Where do they take it and does their grade or credit count?
4. See Articulation Powerpoint<https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.sandiegounified.org/schools/la-jolla/course-planningschedule-changes&sa=D&ust=1562009432470000> slides on Summer School (3 total.)
5. My student has an IEP, who do I contact to make sure that we are picking appropriate teachers and classes for his abilities?
6. Your student’s counselor will be able to assist with most of his classes. The special education team will be reviewing all students’ course requests prior to school starting and will help in making any adjustments in the best interest of the student.
7. My student wants to take Honors Chemistry but it is not listed on the form presented to students but it is listed in the Academic Handbook? What is the process?
8. Students meeting the pre-reqs are eligible to take the class. All students must select an alternate science course backup. Your student should speak to their counselor.
9. My student is fluent in Spanish. He did not take Latin at Muirlands. If he takes the LOTE test what is he supposed to do for a language requirement for college if he can not take Latin?
10. The LOTE test only meets high school graduation requirements. To be eligible to apply to a four year college, students must complete the second year of a foreign language (3-4.) Students can meet college language requirements by taking the SAT Language Subject test or AP exam. See: http://admission.universityofcalifornia.edu/freshman/requirements/a-g-requirements/index.html<https://www.google.com/url?q=http://admission.universityofcalifornia.edu/freshman/requirements/a-g-requirements/index.html&sa=D&ust=1562009432471000>
11. My child did not go to Muirlands. How am I supposed to decide on seminar and math classes as nothing correlates?
12. The registrar and/or counselor will be reviewing all new students’ transcripts to help make course selections and ensure appropriate placement.

FAQ SHEET – SUMMER – 2019

1. What is the difference between Enrollment, Registration and Orientation?
2. Enrollment – enrolling your student who is not enrolled at La Jolla High School into the school
3. Returning students do not need to re-enroll
4. Registration – registering your student for the current year (new ID, new locker, new classes, new books, required annual paperwork etc.)
5. Orientation – for new students and parents meet to get general information about the staff and the school.
6. When is registration?
7. Senior registration: Monday, August 19th from 8:00-12:00 (see designated time below)
8. Junior registration: Tuesday, August 20st from 8:00-12:00 (see designated time below)
9. Sophomore registration: Wednesday, August 21nd from 8:00-12:00 (see designated time below)
10. Freshman registration/orientation: Thursday, August 22rd from 8:00-12:30 (see designated time below)
Note: Please come at designated time for registration:
A – C 8:00 am
D – H 8:30 am
I – M 9:00 am
N – R 9:30 am
S – Z 10:00 am

For more information, see the LJHS website under registration at: https://www.sandiegounified.org/schools/la-jolla<https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.sandiegounified.org/schools/la-jolla&sa=D&ust=1562009432474000> see registration link on the column on the left side.
3. What are the school office hours during the summer?
4. The hours the office will be open are 7:30 – 3:30
5. The office will be open every weekday until July 12th
6. It will be closed from July 13th through August 8th
7. The office will reopen on August 9th
8. Senior Portraits are to be taken over the summer before senior year.
Prestige will be photographing at:
Prestige Portraits Studio
9845 Pasar, San Diego, CA 92126
July 23 –August 4

Go online to confirm your appointment at schedule.prestigeportraits.com

What are the hours the finance office is open for business?
1. Closed for site construction – Please contact Garlepp Eckermann Rosemarie reckermann@sandi.net<mailto:reckermann@sandi.net>

2. Summer Dates
1. Open until July 12th
2. Closed July 13 – August 10
3. Re-open August 13th
4. Regular school year:
5. Monday – Friday
6. Before School 7:05 am – 7:20 am;
7. Lunch 11:34 am – 12:09 pm;
8. After School 2:15 pm – 2:30 pm
9. What can I purchase at the finance office?
10. SAC Card – (printed on ID card);
11. PE Uniforms;
12. Optional Materials for Ceramics Class;
13. Optional Materials for Woodshop Class;
14. Dance Tickets;
15. Theater Play Tickets;
16. CSF Dues;
17. PSAT Exams for Juniors Only;
18. Replacement IDs;
19. Senior Ads for Yearbook;
20. Graduation Tickets
21. What is a SAC Card?
22. An SAC (Student Activity Card):
23. Cost - $30.00 (IF you pre-purchase online before school starts you will also get an LJHS t-shirt.
24. The SAC card gets you:
25. Into sports home - regular season games for free
26. This includes football and basketball.
27. Does not include CIF playoff games
28. Discounted prices on 2 school dances:
29. Homecoming
30. ASB Ball
31. Athletic Letters, emblems and bars
32. What types of payment are accepted at the finance office?
33. Cash or Checks Made Out to La Jolla High School.
34. Credit or Debit Cards are not accepted.
35. What is the Webstore?
36. The Webstore is another way to purchase some of the items listed above (SAC Stickers; Materials for Ceramics and Woodshop Class; Dance Tickets; Senior Ads for Yearbook).
37. What types of payment are accepted at the Webstore?
38. Credit and Debit Cards
39. How do I access the Webstore?
40. There are two ways:
41. Use this website for direct access
https://webstores.activenetwork.com/school-software/la_jolla_high_school/<https://www.google.com/url?q=https://webstores.activenetwork.com/school-software/la_jolla_high_school/&sa=D&ust=1562009432480000>
2. Use La Jolla High School website
https://www.sandiegounified.org/schools/la-jolla<https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.sandiegounified.org/schools/la-jolla&sa=D&ust=1562009432481000>
Go to Home Page, Scroll Down to Webstore then Click on Link for Direct Access
12. How do I sign on to Webstore?
13. **Username = Student ID Number
14. **Password = Student’s First Initial immediately followed by Last Name (ALL lower case; no spacing in between)
15. PLEASE do NOT create a different username/password to make purchases on the Webstore
16. When Buying for Siblings make individual purchases by signing on to each specific student.
17. What Date will the Webstore be opened prior Registration?
18. The webstore is being updated with 2018-2019 information
19. It will be reopened for business on August 14, 2018
20. What can I purchase during registration and how much does it cost?
21. SAC Stickers - $30.00
22. PE Uniforms - $22.00 (shirt and shorts); $10.00 (shirt); $12.00 (short)
23. How Do I Purchase a Yearbook?
24. Starting this year, we are using an outside company that will handle all sales of yearbooks. Further details to come prior to registration.
25. What do I do if I forgot my sign in information to the PowerSchool Student and Parent Sign In Portal?
26. If you forget your user name and/or password for accessing the PowerSchool Student and Parent Sign In you will need to contact the school Site Technician at 858 454 3081 ext. 2209 or via email. Gantman Emily egantman@sandi.net<mailto:egantman@sandi.net>

17. I have a school library book. Can I bring it in before registration next year?
18. Yes! Please do! The library is short textbooks for next year, so we need every book back. If you thought that you had lost your book and paid for it and have since found it, bring it in! You’ll probably get a refund.
19. If you have a book for the coming semester checked out to you, you may keep it for the semester your course is complete
20. Is there summer reading for any classes next year?
21. Summer reading:
22. Pleasure reading is important. Encourage your student to choose challenging books that they would enjoy reading.
23. The whole idea is to get the students to enjoy picking up a book and reading it.
24. No assigned summer reading this year except for AP students.
25. The list was given to the student before they left for summer break.
26. How do the lockers work? Do I have to have one? Do I have to buy a lock?
27. LJHS provides lockers for students who choose to use one.
28. Locks are also provided. They are already on the lockers
29. Use the school provided locks. Do not bring a different lock
30. Combinations will be given to students right after they choose their lockers at registration.
31. Again, having a locker is not mandatory this year
32. It is not necessary to purchase a lock for the locker; the locks are already on the lockers.
33. Have my transcripts been sent to my college?
34. All transcripts all being sent on or before July 1
35. I need my Transcripts sent to NCAA
36. Transcripts will be sent by Ms. Lopez to NCAA electronically by July 6
37. Is the Registrar office open?
38. Registrar’s office will be open till July 12
39. Transcripts walk in hours 8am 12pm till July 12
40. Who do I contact if I need transcripts to be email, mailed to me or sent to a school?
41. Email Mrs. Lopez at dlopez1@sandi.net
42. Provide your Last, First, Middle Names while attending La Jolla High School, Date of Birth,
43. Year of graduation or years attended LJHS and a photocopy of an ID ex. Drivers license, military ID or passport
44. Where can I get transcripts after July 12?
45. After July 12 please contact the:
Quality of Assurance Office
Eugene Brucker Education Center
4100 Normal Street, Anx. 10
San Diego, CA 92103
Phone: (619) 278-6732
Fax: (619) 725-8097
26. I need a work permit, where can I get one
27. Work permit: are available at:
The Work Permit Office
IMC-Building E
2441 Cardinal Lane
San Diego, CA 92123
858-503-1750
27. I didn’t pick up my Diploma at Graduation, can I still pick it up?
28. Yes, you can come by the Registrars officer till July 12 from 8am-12pm.
29. Athletics - How do I go about participating in a School Sport?
30. Every athlete must go on line and complete the athletic clearance process before trying out for a team. The link for this is: https://ljvikings.com/athletic-clearance-2/<https://www.google.com/url?q=https://ljvikings.com/athletic-clearance-2/&sa=D&ust=1562009432489000>
Please take the time to watch quick tutorial video. It helps
2. You will not be allowed to try-out, practice, or participate until all steps have been completed and you have received a clearance email from the aathleticclearance.com<https://www.google.com/url?q=http://aathleticclearance.com/&sa=D&ust=1562009432490000> system.
3. In order to compete in athletics at La Jolla High School, you must comply with each of the following steps.
4. Complete all parts of the Athletics Clearance Online Forms.
5. (OPTIONAL) Purchase an SAC (Student Activity Card) card from the school at a cost of $30.00. The SAC card gets you into all home regular season games.
6. Submit The SDUSD Physician's Physical Forms and the Consent Form to the administration in the main office once you have completed the online forms process. Or, upload the SDUSD Physical Forms and the Consent Form online. The SDSUD Physical Form is the ONLY accepted form.
7. Receive an email stating that you are cleared to play.
8. For the sports year 2019-20, ALL PHYSICALS MUST be AFTER June 4, 2018

29. What are the different Athletics seasons?
1. Fall Sports:
2. Cross Country
3. Football
4. Girls Golf
5. Girls Volleyball
6. Field Hockey
7. Boys Water Polo
8. Girls Tennis, Cheer
9. Winter Sports:
10. Girls Basketball
11. Boys Basketball
12. Girls Soccer
13. Boys Soccer
14. Wrestling

  2. Purchase Order

  5. Payment

On Wed, Jun 19, 2019 at 11:27 AM Michael Leonetti <mleonetti@getsonarcloud.com> wrote:

Hi all and good morning,


We just took a look at the configuration of the phone where SonarCloud is installed at Grady. We were able to see the issue with the phone as Lynn described. When we arrived the display and calling in from classrooms did not work.


However, when we unplugged the phone and plugged it back in it started working again. Then when we tried that again, it stopped working!


The results were the same with the phone plugged directly into the jack or with the splitter that we installed for SonarCloud.


It looks like the cause of the issue is either the the jack itself or something on the PA end. Because the intermittent issue is the same with the phone plugged directly in and with the splitter (AKA with AND without SonarCloud installed), we do not believ this to be a SonarCloud issue.


We left Lynn with instructions on how to revive it if it breaks again, but it seems to be a temperamental hardware issue.


I hope this is helpful.


Michael A. Leonetti

Intercom

Scheduled Database Maintenance - App Downtime

Upcoming scheduled maintenance noticeBetween 2019-06-19 0700 UTC and 2019-06-19 0730 UTC, Intercom will be unavailable to access due to some maintenance required on our core database services.

What is the impact?
Our main database cluster will be entirely down for a period of time. To facilitate a safe change, we will also be removing all web/API server capacity. This will impact all Intercom features, and they will not be accessible during the downtime.

How long will the downtime last?
Intercom will be fully unavailable for all customers during the maintenance window while we perform the change. Once the change is complete we will then start to scale back up our server fleets and start serving requests again. During this recovery time, Intercom will be unavailable to some but not all customers. Some but not all message delivery may be delayed.

What will the exact experience be for our customers during the change?
Team mates already in the Intercom app - will receive an Intercom error message in their browsers and will not be able to use the platform.
Team mates trying to load the Intercom app - will receive a generic 503 “service unavailable” message in their browser
End users on a website where the Intercom messenger is installed - will experience the messenger appearing, but the components in the messenger will not load and/or be available to interact with
Developers trying to use the API - will receive a 503 “service unavailable” error in their response
What will happen messages that are scheduled to send during this time?
They will be delayed for the duration of the downtime.

What will happen to e-mails that get sent in?
They will be queued up and processed/delivered once the platform is back up. Start time Jun 19, 07:00 UTC Estimated duration 1 hour Components affected Intercom Messenger - Web MessengerIntercom Messenger - Mobile MessengerIntercom Web ApplicationIntercom APIsIntercom Mobile APIs

...and 5 more components.

View full scheduled maintenance details

source.subject: Inquiry On Sonarcloud - Christiana Owusu-Ampaw
source.body:
Hello,


I hope this email finds you well. My name is Christiana Owusu-Ampaw and I am a student at New Visions Charter High School For Advanced Math and Science. A group of seniors and I are conducting an experiment on our school bell system. Instead of our regular bell system, we decided to play different genres of music. We are aware that your company focuses on bell systems and we would love to learn more about it.


My group noticed that there is a strong correlation between the school bell system and the prison bell system. Thus, rather than encouraging a sound as the bell sound, we are trying to switch to music as the bell sound. After conducting an experiment, we are encouraged that students are more motivated to go to class after hearing to music that they are familiar to.


We would love to have a conversation with you to learn more about your company and how you work with bell systems. We would really love to see a future with this project because we believe there need to be changes in the school system as a whole.


Thank you so much and hope to hear from you soon.


You could reach me through this email or at 917-891-5610.


Sincerely,

Christiana Owusu-Ampaw

source.subject: Important - issues with DOE schools and Sonarcloud - FIXED!
source.body:
Good morning Mateo,

As of early last week, there seem to be sporadic issues accessing our services for a good deal of DOE schools. They appears as any of the following:

  • Cannot log into the Sonarcloud App or Dashboard (dashboard.getsonarcloud.com)
  • The Sonarcloud App hangs when sending announcements 
  • Sent announcements are not playing over the PA system
  • The Sonarcloud announcement phone will not make announcements

It turns out that DIIT/DOE is slowly migrating over all DOE schools to a new firewall. In the process, one of the firewalls had mistakenly blocked our main server address (maestro.s0nr.co).

We are happy to report that because of your diligent efforts in contacting DIIT and putting in trouble tickets the issue is now solved! Late in the school day yesterday the block had been removed. We immediately saw all offline Sonarcloud devices come back up. Also, nearly immediately, schools messaged us saying all is well. This was music to our ears!
​

We want to thank you for being a valuable part of the Sonarcloud family. We could not have done it without you.

Thank you again and have a FANTASTIC day!
​

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (Q308 PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (Q308 PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

source.subject: Important - issues with DOE schools and Sonarcloud - FIXED!
source.body:
Good morning Kirk,

As of early last week, there seem to be sporadic issues accessing our services for a good deal of DOE schools. They appears as any of the following:

  • Cannot log into the Sonarcloud App or Dashboard (dashboard.getsonarcloud.com)
  • The Sonarcloud App hangs when sending announcements 
  • Sent announcements are not playing over the PA system
  • The Sonarcloud announcement phone will not make announcements

It turns out that DIIT/DOE is slowly migrating over all DOE schools to a new firewall. In the process, one of the firewalls had mistakenly blocked our main server address (maestro.s0nr.co).

We are happy to report that because of your diligent efforts in contacting DIIT and putting in trouble tickets the issue is now solved! Late in the school day yesterday the block had been removed. We immediately saw all offline Sonarcloud devices come back up. Also, nearly immediately, schools messaged us saying all is well. This was music to our ears!
​

We want to thank you for being a valuable part of the Sonarcloud family. We could not have done it without you.

Thank you again and have a FANTASTIC day!
​

Sent: Wednesday, October 10, 2018 6:33 PM
To: Christie Chow <cchow@kingscollegiate.org>
Subject: Introducing SonarCloud School Communication per Christopher Padmore

Good Afternoon Christine,

Mr. Padmore of the Middle School for Arts & Philosophy is having our service installed next Monday and specifically asked us to reach out to you since you're at the same location. Also, left you a message earlier today.

At Sonarcloud we integrate existing PAs (we did one from 1960) with new ones. We connect our device to PA systems and give you the ability to schedule and make announcements from any device, anywhere, extend them with SMS to parent/staff capabilities (with real-time translation), announce to smart display devices and more. We built Sonarcloud to help schools improve communication and safety while also helping them maximize spend.

A few questions to determine next steps in our process, pricing, etc if you'd like more specific info:

  • How to you currently make announcements- phone or microphone? phone
  • If telephone, what is the type? Polycom
  • If possible, would you please forward us a picture of your unit (with brand name/logo)? Attached.
  • If Sonarcloud Connect is of interest, how many smart display boards do you have? N/A
  • Are there any other questions we can answer regarding Sonarcloud specific to you?

I believe you did this in the old South Shore building which houses one of our sister schools, Uncommon Leadership Charter School and the building uses your application in case that is helpful as you think about how to connect our phones (they have the same phone and announcement system as we do).

The pricing is straightforward:

$799 One-time charge that includes device installation, configuration, account setup, & training

$899/yr for the service

$49/board/yr if you decide to do Sonarcloud Connect to announce to smart display boards

That's it.

Again, we'll be onsite next Monday, so if you decide you're in we'll get you all set up that day at the same time as Chris's service.

Thanks again for your time, and hope to hear from you soon.

source.subject: SONARCLOUD Installation: Option #2
source.body:
Michael,

We need to do option #2. When can you or your field team come to the school to install and/or configure the equipment?

We can't do any live over the PA System testing until 4pm everyday.


We've attached Sonarcloud to the Trunk port in the system and we've seen that it works. HOWEVER, the system cannot work with both Sonarcloud AND your VoIP phone system. We've seen that setting the system to one of them will disable the other.

So there are two basic solutions at this point. Let me list the quicker one and what I believe to be the easier one first. Although "easy" can be a relative term.

1. Since your VoIP system is already integrated with your PA, we can become a VoIP phone on your network. This is an easy solution where we could integrate the Sonarcloud device as a SIP phone just like every other phone on your network. Just like your phones now, we can dial the extension to make announcements. This would require your VoIP company provisioning us another "line" or "extension" or whatever terminology they use for another SIP phone. We would just need the SIP credentials for it from your VoIP provider. We can talk directly to the people who do your VoIP phones to make things go smoother. This can be done remotely and ASAP since we already have a Sonarcloud device on-site.

2. If number 1 doesn't work, it is possible to integrate physically into the system. We'd have to find a date to come back and integrate a piece of hardware Tim thinks is already there on-site and unused.

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (Woodstown HS PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (Woodstown HS PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (Highbridge PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (Highbridge PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

Hello JP,

Thank you for your help and willingness in this.

Just to sum up what we've tried so far.

We've attached Sonarcloud to the Trunk port in the system and we've seen that it works. HOWEVER, the system cannot work with both Sonarcloud AND your VoIP phone system. We've seen that setting the system to one of them will disable the other.

So there are two basic solutions at this point. Let me list the quicker one and what I believe to be the easier one first. Although "easy" can be a relative term.

1. Since your VoIP system is already integrated with your PA, we can become a VoIP phone on your network. This is an easy solution where we could integrate the Sonarcloud device as a SIP phone just like every other phone on your network. Just like your phones now, we can dial the extension to make announcements. This would require your VoIP company provisioning us another "line" or "extension" or whatever terminology they use for another SIP phone. We would just need the SIP credentials for it from your VoIP provider. We can talk directly to the people who do your VoIP phones to make things go smoother. This can be done remotely and ASAP since we already have a Sonarcloud device on-site.

2. If number 1 doesn't work, it is possible to integrate physically into the system. We'd have to find a date to come back and integrate a piece of hardware Tim thinks is already there on-site and unused.

Please let me know if this makes sense! Hope to speak to you soon!

Hello JP,

Thank you for your help and willingness in this.

Just to sum up what we've tried so far.

We've attached Sonarcloud to the Trunk port in the system and we've seen that it works. HOWEVER, the system cannot work with both Sonarcloud AND your VoIP phone system. We've seen that setting the system to one of them will disable the other.

So there are two basic solutions at this point. Let me list the quicker one and what I believe to be the easier one first. Although "easy" can be a relative term.

1. Since your VoIP system is already integrated with your PA, we can become a VoIP phone on your network. This is an easy solution where we could integrate the Sonarcloud device as a SIP phone just like every other phone on your network. Just like your phones now, we can dial the extension to make announcements. This would require your VoIP company provisioning us another "line" or "extension" or whatever terminology they use for another SIP phone. We would just need the SIP credentials for it from your VoIP provider. We can talk directly to the people who do your VoIP phones to make things go smoother. This can be done remotely and ASAP since we already have a Sonarcloud device on-site.

2. If number 1 doesn't work, it is possible to integrate physically into the system. We'd have to find a date to come back and integrate a piece of hardware Tim thinks is already there on-site and unused.

Please let me know if this makes sense! Hope to speak to you soon!

--

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device is down. Please note
that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make
announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go
through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device
back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building.
Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online
and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these
aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send
announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud
device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it.
This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building.
Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android
cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in.
The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and
dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to
see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot
further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

--

Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (BHSA PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

Please also see the article on troubleshooting here: http://help.getsonarcloud.com/troubleshooting/announcements-arent-playing

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

On 11/14/18 2:10 PM, Michael A. Leonetti wrote:

Hi Chris,

Let me answer your questions as best I could.

1. Does Raspberrypi device have to be natted.

The Sonarcloud device requires accessing our servers outside, so yes. We'll need outbound.

2. Sonar Cloud Server farm IP prefix.

The IP address of our servers are sparse. You can use 107.170.9.252, or the domain maestro.s0nr.co which will always resolve to the correct.

3. NTP pool to be used.

We are using *.debian.pool.ntp.org (in the form of 0.debian.pool.ntp.org, 1.debian.pool.ntp.org, etc)

4. Internal IP address of Raspberry pi.

We didn't pre-emptively set a static IP address for the Pi. If we can get the Pi online temporarily we can set an IP address, or alternatively, you could find the Mac address on your network and enforce a DHCP IP address. That might be the easiest.

5. Confirmation that root access to the Raspberry Pi has been removed.

If this is necessary, we can do this. However, root is secured with a 64 byte password and not utilized by the Sonarcloud software.

Hope this is helpful. Let me know if you have any other questions.

Michael A. Leonetti As warm as green tea Co-Founder, Sonarcloud 718-407-0664, Ext. 100 http://getsonarcloud.com Note: For a faster response to issues please e-mail support@getsonarcloud.com

On 10/16/2018 10:14 AM, Michael A. Leonetti wrote:

Good morning Chris,

Thank you for reaching back out.

Let me answer your inquiries.

1. Web application security testing report aka (penetration testing)

We don't have any web application security reports. You are welcome to run however many you'd like to your satisfaction. If you know of a good service you use, let us know and we'll generate some reports off of it to meet your security standards.

As you can probably already see, the device tries to connect to maestro.s0nr.co (as well as NTP pools). maestro.s0nr.co has no web interface and doesn't run a normal web service. The ports you'll find open on it are only for our custom protocols, websockets, and monitoring.

2. Application Architecture diagram.

3. System Architecture diagram.

You'll see a diagram of how our product works attached to the e-mail. It's rather simplistic, but our system is of a rather simple design.

4. Security of physical devices installed in our network ( OS, built, patching, antivirus, SSL etc. )

It's a RaspberryPi with Raspian (Stretch), based on Debian Stretch. It does not contain an antivirus, as it is not accessible to the user for any type of file/network storage. The Pi device contains our proprietary software that you'll see connecting via TLS/TCP to ports 6523 (communication), 6524 (data), and 6527 (maintenance) exclusively to maestro.s0nr.co. Feel free to restrict as such.

Also, if you'd like to give us your custom NTP server, we can use that to sync time with.


Lastly, we do have a web application (dashboard.getsonarcloud.com). This is where bells can be scheduled and announcements can be made to the PA system also. It only uses standard web ports and websockets (all over HTTPS), but I wanted to add it for your consideration.


Hope this is helpful! Thank you for your quick response. Feel free to ask me any more questions as needed.

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (PS 356 PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (PS 356 PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.

If both of those things work, please try rebooting your Sonarcloud device. This device is a little device with our Sonarcloud logo on it. This device will be plugged into the power (AC outlet) of your building. Please locate the small power cable (which almost looks like an Android cell phone charger). Next, unplug it from the wall and plug it back in. The Sonarcloud device should come up within a minute. Your App and dashboard should alert you when this happens. We will also be able to see it.

If this doesn't work, please reach out to us and we can troubleshoot further.

Thank you and have a fantastic day!

Hello JP,

Just to sum up what we've tried so far.

We've attached Sonarcloud to the Trunk port in the system and we've seen that it works. HOWEVER, the system cannot work with both Sonarcloud AND your VoIP phone system. We've seen that setting the system to one of them will disable the other.

So there are two basic solutions at this point. Let me list the quicker one and what I believe to be the easier one first. Although "easy" can be a relative term.

1. Since your VoIP system is already integrated with your PA, we can become a VoIP phone on your network. This is an easy solution where we could integrate the Sonarcloud device as a SIP phone just like every other phone on your network. Just like your phones now, we can dial the extension to make announcements. This would require your VoIP company provisioning us another "line" or "extension" or whatever terminology they use for another SIP phone. We would just need the SIP credentials for it from your VoIP provider. We can talk directly to the people who do your VoIP phones to make things go smoother. This can be done remotely and ASAP since we already have a Sonarcloud device on-site.

2. If number 1 doesn't work, it is possible to integrate physically into the system. We'd have to find a date to come back and integrate a piece of hardware Tim thinks is already there on-site and unused.

Please let me know if this makes sense! Hope to speak to you soon!

source.subject: Your Sonarcloud device (Q308 PA System) is down - Troubleshooting
source.body:
Hello!

We are getting alerts that your Sonarcloud device (Q308 PA System) is down. Please note that while the Sonarcloud device is down you will not be able to make announcements through the device. I'd like to take a moment to go through with you some troubleshooting steps to try and get the device back up and running so that you can make announcements.

Firstly, let's check if there is Internet and power in your building. Please check the computers to make sure that you are able to get online and that the lights are working in the building. If either of these aren't working, unfortunately, currently, Sonarcloud won't send announcements either.
